about: The evangelium of the formulary “Septuagesima Sunday” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus told His disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven is like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire laborers into his vineyard. Having agreed with the laborers on a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard. Going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace and said to them: You also go into my vineyard, and I will give you whatever is fair. And they went their way. Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hours and did likewise. But about the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and says to them: Why do you stand here idle all day? They say to him: Because no one has hired us. He says to them: You also go into my vineyard. And when evening had come, the lord of the vineyard says to his steward: Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last up to the first. When those who had arrived about the eleventh hour came, they received a denarius each. But when the first also came, they thought they would receive more; but they too received a denarius each. On receiving it, they murmured against the householder, saying: These last have worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and of heat. But he answered one of them, saying: Friend, I do you no wrong. Did you not agree with me on a denarius? Take what is yours and go your way; but I want to give this last worker the same as you. Or is it not lawful for me to do what I want? Is your eye evil because I am good? So the last will be first and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.

a.g: Jesus told His disciples this parable:
The kingdom of heaven is like a householder
Having agreed with the laborers on a denarius a day,
I will give you whatever is fair
But about the eleventh hour he went out
Why do you stand here idle all day?
And when evening had come, the lord of the vineyard says to his steward:
When those who had arrived about the eleventh hour came, they received a denarius each
But when the first also came, they thought
but they too received a denarius each

you have made them equal to us
the burden of the day and of heat

Did you not agree with me on a denarius?
but I want to give this last worker the same as you

ex.w061: The future dabo supports a future-perfect reading of fúerit. The same form can also be perfect subjunctive, so the mood remains uncertain here.
ex.w179: The selected genitive singular takes æstus with diei as dependents of pondus: the burden of the day and of heat. The same form can also be accusative plural, coordinated with pondus as another object of portavimus. The choice remains uncertain.
ex.w205: Huic refers to the last worker whom the householder wants to pay the same as the person addressed. Hence masculine. The form itself permits all three genders and does not establish this reference without context.
